title: Short qudit triorthogonal codes from doubling
abstract: We construct short triorthogonal codes for qudits of odd prime dimension by generalizing doubling, which combines a triorthogonal code with a code admitting a transversal phase gate, and raises the distance by up to two. This gives codes with parameters $[[28,1,4]]_3$, $[[37,1,5]]_3$, $[[72,1,6]]_3$, $[[118,1,8]]_3$, $[[33,1,5]]_5$ and $[[20,1,4]]_7$, each shorter than the cyclic, concatenated and Reed-Muller codes of the same distance, and a doubling construction of the $[[15,1,3]]_3$ code. When the columns of a generator matrix are regarded as charged points, triorthogonality becomes the vanishing of multipole moments up to octupole order, and doubling becomes a double layer of opposite charges; this picture explains why inputs with nontrivial coefficients can give shorter codes. We also show by exhaustive search that the shortest codes of distance three have length $11$ for $p=5$ and length $7$ for $p=7$. Combined with high-rate distance-two codes, the new codes reduce the cost of qutrit magic state distillation by up to an order of magnitude in regimes with high input noise.
summary: This paper introduces a novel 'doubling' construction method to create short, high-distance triorthogonal quantum error-correcting codes for qudits. By generalizing known techniques, the authors derive specific code parameters that outperform existing constructions. These codes are particularly valuable for reducing the resource cost in quantum state distillation protocols.
main_problem: The paper focuses on constructing short qudit triorthogonal quantum error-correcting codes for qudits of odd prime dimension.
main_result: The authors developed a 'doubling' construction that yields several short codes, such as $[[28, 1, 4]]_3$, which are shorter than existing codes of comparable distance.
method: The construction generalizes the doubling procedure by combining a triorthogonal seed code with a P-code (a code admitting a transversal phase gate), analyzed through algebraic and geometric moment vanishing conditions.
model_or_system: The underlying model is the theory of qudit quantum error correction, specifically focusing on triorthogonal codes which incorporate a transversal third-level diagonal gate. The physical application is improving qutrit magic state distillation.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]_p$ (length, dimension, distance), and the vanishing of multipole moments (up to octupole order) for the charge distribution representation.
important_parameters: Odd prime dimension $p$, and the code distance $d$. The construction yields distance $d = \min(d_P, d_T + 2)$.
main_assumptions: The construction assumes the existence of a P-code $S$ and a seed $T$, and the geometric interpretation relates triorthogonality to the vanishing of multipole moments.
figures_summary: The notes mention numerous listings and matrices of constructed codes (P-codes, Seeds, Doubled codes) for various parameters, detailing the resulting code parameters.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the problem (triorthogonal codes) to introducing the core technique (doubling construction via Theorem 4), providing the mathematical framework (geometric interpretation via moments), and finally presenting specific, optimized code examples and bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, mathematically rigorous constructions for high-performance quantum error-correcting codes tailored for qudits, which is crucial for scaling up quantum computation beyond qubits.
